# Horsens Kirurgi

Horsens Kirurgi is a surgical department whose quality performance is tracked through the DANIBD (Danish Inflammatory Bowel Disease Database) national registry. The department's surgical quality is measured using a re-operation indicator, which assesses the proportion of patients requiring repeat surgery within 30 days of their initial surgical procedure—a key metric for evaluating surgical safety and technique [^src1].

As of the 2024 assessment year, Horsens Kirurgi reported a re-operation rate of 0 percent for surgical procedures, placing the department well below the national development target of 8 percent [^src1]. This performance indicates that none of the surgical patients treated at Horsens Kirurgi required re-operation within the 30-day post-operative window during the measurement period, positioning the department favorably within the national quality-assurance framework for inflammatory bowel disease treatment.

The re-operation indicator is one of two major quality metrics tracked in the DANIBD system. The other measures the proportion of inflammatory bowel disease patients receiving annual F-calprotectin testing as part of their biological medication monitoring protocol. Together, these indicators provide a comprehensive picture of surgical and medical care quality for patients with inflammatory bowel disease across Danish health regions [^src1].
